title: Add English/Hebrew i18n provider with logical-property RTL layout
context: The commit message does not state a motivation. The change introduces Hebrew UI support, which previously was not present: the app had no i18n layer and its layout was LTR-only. Font loading was also tied to online access, which the commit addresses separately.
decision: Added an I18nProvider/useI18n layer with English and Hebrew locales. A language switch in the header is persisted in localStorage and defaults to Hebrew when the browser is Hebrew. The provider sets <html lang> and <html dir> and the page title. Layout uses logical CSS properties throughout. Arrow-key tab navigation and the back arrow mirror in RTL, directional icons use a flip-rtl class, and play/stop/record icons are not mirrored. Dates and durations get bidi isolation, and transcripts lay out in their own language's direction.
consequences: Every user-visible string must go through the locale files (src/locales/en.js and src/locales/he.js), so new strings need both translations.
Direction is set on the document root at runtime, so RTL behavior depends on the provider being mounted above all tabs.
Directional icons need the flip-rtl class to mirror correctly. Icons that are not directional must not get it.
Hebrew glyph coverage now relies on the system font stack (Segoe UI first), since the Google Fonts link was removed for offline use.
Persisted language is per browser through localStorage, not per account.
